doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Playing with Wynton Marsalis and Wycliffe Gordon
summary: Raph recalls a Lincoln Center Mulligan tribute, Wynton's warmth and Wycliffe Gordon's playing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Cool. My goodness. Wynton Marsalis you’ve played behind?

Yes. Once. Yeah it was wonderful. I was so nervous. I got a call from Art Baron that he recommended me for a Wynton Marsalis Lincoln Center concert because they were doing the music of Gerry Mulligan. And I was to play tuba and bass trombone. So I went and I went into Carroll Studios with the tuba and the bass bone and I just sat there very quietly and Wynton came in and there was sort of a lull so I went up to him and I said, “Excuse me” I said “my name is Alan Raph,” and the next thing I know he’s hugging me. It was the warmest thing. I thought oh my God. So immediately I fell in love with Wynton. Then I saw the way he rehearsed the band and the way he worked and it was on the money. It was just so good. I enjoyed a lot working with him, and I enjoyed almost as much, in a different way, meeting Wycliffe Gordon. Wycliffe — you look at him and you just don’t think he’s going to get that trombone in his face fast enough to play, because he doesn’t set, he picks up the horn and he’s playing like this. And then he’s off in space somewhere and the next thing you know he’s playing again. You don’t see this kind of setting up guys do. And he plays astoundingly well. And he’s incredibly good. So I listened to that, I listened to him play the sousaphone and we got talking a little bit and at one point I brought in that book that I gave you, “Le Trombone” it’s kind of a funny book that I did that’s out on the market. I gave him a copy of that. He brought me a CD that he did with somebody else. And we got talking. He said to me, he says, “Hey I’ve got to take a couple a tuba lessons with you.” I says, “Yeah, I’ll teach you everything I know in five minutes.” He is a wonderful tuba player and just an outstanding trombone player. I enjoyed it. It was a nice week. It was just a week.
